x: The Mulki rules belong to the Nizam's era: they date from 1888 and were tightened by the Nizam's farman of 1919, allowing only residents of about 15 years to get local jobs. 12 years was the domicile period in the 1956 Gentlemen's Agreement, and the rules were neither British nor post-Independence.

The Socialists' joint Andhra-Hyderabad meeting was at Kurnool on 21-22 March 1954. 13-14 June 1954, Hyderabad was the second Mahasabha (not the APCC, which met at Kurnool on 30 Sep 1953); 12-13 Feb 1950, Warangal was the first Mahasabha session, not the second; 26 Nov 1949, Vijayawada was the founding of the Visalandhra Mahasabha rather than its first session.

All three apply: Ayyadevara Kaleswara Rao founded the Visalandhra Mahasabha at Vijayawada on 26 Nov 1949, raised the demand at the 1951 Bangalore Congress manifesto meeting, and resigned when no decision came.

All three are correct: Article 371D, inserted by the 32nd Amendment (1973) to implement the Six-Point Formula, provides equitable opportunities in public employment and education, local cadres and the AP Administrative Tribunal.
